catalogue.name: Purchase.Order.Pdf
catalogue.description: Prints a purchase order as a PDF document and writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up.
catalogue.selectionDescription: Get an open purchase order as a PDF, printed with the vendor's report selection for usage P.Order. Increases the order's No. Printed and, when an interaction template is set up, writes an interaction log entry. For a sales order confirmation use Sales.OrderConfirmation.Pdf; for any other report use Orchestrator.Report.SaveAs.

strict.description: Optional root Boolean, default false. When true, unknown data keys are refused before execution with UnknownParameter. Do not place this option inside data.

subject.description: The purchase order: its SystemId (a GUID) or its No.

target.description: A GUID is read as the SystemId of the purchase order, anything else as its No.
Read the same way as subject.
Read the same way as subject.
Read the same way as subject.
Read the same way as subject.

parameters.name: orderNo
parameters.description: The No. or the SystemId of the purchase order. Needed when subject is empty.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The SystemId or the No. of the purchase order.

parameters.name: documentNo
parameters.description: Same as orderNo, for callers that use the generic document keys.

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: Same as orderId, for callers that use the generic document keys.

fields.name: binary
fields.description: The PDF file of the purchase order itself, not JSON. A client such as MCP hands it on as base64.

fields.name: datacontenttype
fields.description: application/pdf with a quoted name parameter containing PurchaseOrder-<SystemId>.pdf. The SystemId is lowercase without braces; this stable filename contains no unsafe document-number characters. Playbooks expose the same MIME value as contentType.

errors.error: Read permission denied for purchase orders.
errors.when: The caller has no read permission on Purchase Header.
errors.fix: Ask an administrator to grant read access to Purchase Header.

errors.when: subject, orderNo, orderId, documentNo and documentId are all empty.
errors.fix: Send the order No. or SystemId as subject or as data.orderNo.

errors.when: No purchase document of type Order has that No. or SystemId. Quotes, invoices, blanket orders and posted documents are not orders.
errors.fix: Find the order with Data.Records.Get on Purchase Header filtered on Document Type Order.

errors.error: The identifiers name different purchase orders.
errors.when: Two of subject, orderNo, orderId, documentNo and documentId point at different orders.
errors.fix: Send one identifier, or identifiers of the same order.

errors.error: No report is set up for Report Selections usage P.Order.
errors.when: Neither Report Selections nor the vendor's document layouts name a report for the purchase order.
errors.fix: Set up a purchase order report in Report Selection - Purchase, usage Order.

errors.when: The report fails while rendering, for example a layout error.
errors.fix: Read the text and correct the report layout or the order.

errors.when: A transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. The error preserves Business Central's original text. Uncaught errors are Retryable only for types with effect write.
errors.fix: Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed.

effect.changes: Increases No. Printed on the purchase order and, when an interaction template is set up for purchase orders, writes an interaction log entry for the vendor's contact: the standard report does both. It may also archive a version of the order when Purchases & Payables Setup archives orders. A replacement report in Report Selections may not. Saving the PDF commits the work done so far, so the call cannot run inside a larger transaction that is rolled back.

related.name: Sales.SalesInvoice.Pdf
related.useInsteadWhen: You need a posted sales document for a customer, not a purchase order.

related.name: Orchestrator.Report.SaveAs
related.useInsteadWhen: You need another report, a format other than PDF or your own request page options.

steps.purpose: Find the purchase order on Purchase Header, filtered on Document Type Order; read its no or id.
Get the purchase order PDF with that no as subject.
Attach the PDF to an e-mail draft for the vendor.

workflow.text: Send a purchase order to the vendor.

chapters.overview: Returns an open purchase order as a PDF, printed with the report the vendor's Report Selection (usage P.Order) names; by default the standard purchase order. Use it to hand the order to the vendor, a person or another system. Printing it increases No. Printed on the order and, when an interaction template is set up for purchase orders, writes an interaction log entry.
chapters.notes: subject and the keys under data (orderNo, orderId, documentNo, documentId) are all tried: a value that looks like a GUID is read as the SystemId, anything else as the No. Only purchase documents of type Order are found. Two identifiers that name different orders are refused with ConflictingIdentifiers. The success MIME type carries name="PurchaseOrder-<SystemId>.pdf"; callers may use that filename when saving the unchanged binary PDF. Only the Success answer is a PDF; an error answer is JSON (text/json). The same read permission on Purchase Header is required as for reading the order. Saving the PDF commits the work done so far, so the call cannot run inside a larger transaction that is rolled back. When an interaction template is set up for purchase orders, the standard report writes an interaction log entry for the vendor's contact. A replacement report in Report Selections may not. The call does not change whether that logging happens.

response.conventions:
## Errors and warnings
An error response has `status` = `Error`, a stable `code`, the `error` text and, when they apply, `parameter` (the request parameter concerned, e.g. `lines[2].no`), `received` (the value received), `expected` (what was expected) and `nextStep` (what to do now). `hint` says where to read more.
When a request has several problems, all of them are listed in `errors[]` - each with the same fields - under a top-level `code` (`MultipleErrors`, or a shared code such as `InvalidLine` for the `lines` of a Create type) and a summary `error`. Fix them all before calling again. One problem is reported at the top level, with no `errors[]`.
Request values are checked first and every problem found is reported together. A Business Central validation error raised afterwards, while a record is being written, stops the call and is reported on its own: `code` = `BusinessCentralError`, Business Central's own `error` text, and `parameter` naming the request parameter being applied, e.g. `lines[1].accountNo`. Nothing is written.
Request values are read in one format, whatever the language: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; date-times ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset; amounts as JSON numbers (or a string such as `"1234.56"`, no thousands separator); integers as JSON integers; booleans `true` or `false`. Any other value is `InvalidParameterFormat` with `received` and `expected`; for an unambiguous local form such as `26.09.2026`, `nextStep` gives the value to resend. Every bad value of a request is reported together.
Answers are written in one format as well, whatever the language of the call: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times ISO 8601, numbers with a dot and no thousands separator, and the option and enum values of every answer except `Data.Records.Get` and `Data.Records.Set` as their English names, so a value read from an answer can be sent back. Those two answer the caption of the language of the call, for a person to read. The language of the call (`lcid`) changes captions and message texts, not these forms. Two things are outside Bifrost's control: Business Central writes its own texts (a ledger entry description such as `Direct Cost V00010 on 10/02/26`, the text of a `BusinessCentralError`) with the regional settings of the server session, which `lcid` does not change, so a date in such a text can be in month-day order; and a table view is read with those settings too, so write dates in a view as `YYYY-MM-DD` and decimals with a dot.
Both success and error responses can carry `warnings[]`, each with `code`, `message` and, when they apply, `parameter` and `nextStep`.
`UnknownParameter` refuses undeclared data keys before execution for every type whose effect is not read, including a missing effect. The root envelope option `strict:false` cannot opt out. Read types keep warnings without changing status, validationResult or domain warningCount unless the caller sets `strict:true` (next to type and subject, never inside data). Refusals list the keys and localized nextStep corrections; no business changes or successful execution charges occur. Example: {"type":"Memory.User.Set","strict":true,"data":{"memory":"test","memry":"typo"}} is refused.
`FieldChangedByBC` is a warning from Data.Records.Set: another field validation or the write changed a sent field after its own validation. `parameter` names data[n].fields.{jsonName}, counting from 0. Status stays Success. Compare the returned values with what you sent; follow `nextStep` to use validation order or send the field again in a separate call. Normalisation of the field itself, LCY, Dimension Set ID, BLOB, Media, MediaSet and skipped fields are excluded.
`SecurityFilterApplied` is a warning from Data.Records.Get, severity `low`, `parameter` `table`: a security filter of the caller applies to the table, so the result may hold fewer records than the table. `securityFiltered` is then true. Status stays Success, and the hidden records are never counted or described. Ask an administrator if you expect more records.
Data.RecordIds.Get, Data.Totals.Get, Data.Entries.Find and CSV.Records.Get do not return `securityFiltered` or `SecurityFilterApplied`. Their results can still be limited by security filters: counts and totals cover only visible records, and the absence of a flag or warning does not prove that every record in the table was included. Their help explains this visibility limit; request filters such as tableView and date ranges are separate.
When a Business Central operation fails, the error can identify the request parameter being applied, the expected input and what to do next. That guidance accompanies the original `BusinessCentralError` after rollback, including a failed queued task. It does not change which writes are rolled back or committed. Guidance is cleared between messages; a message without it keeps its existing response shape. Recognized lock errors follow the `Retryable` rules below.
Some message types accept calls only through a particular path: a scheduled queue message, the Task API (`/tasks`), the in-product MCP tool server, another message type, or the Messages page Run Task action. Bifrost determines where the call came from; request values cannot override it. A call through an unsupported path is refused with `PreconditionFailed` and a `nextStep` naming the path to use.
`Retryable` means a transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. `error` keeps Business Central's original text. `expected` is "no concurrent lock on the same records"; `nextStep` is "Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed." Bifrost does not retry automatically. Uncaught recognized lock errors are also `Retryable` for `write` types. Uncaught `read` and `irreversible` errors remain `BusinessCentralError`, because an irreversible operation may already have committed.
`ConfirmationRequired` is the preview refusal for an irreversible type called without `expectedCount`. Nothing was changed; inspect `expected` and the description before sending the same request with that count. `ConfirmationMismatch` means the count has changed or the sent count was wrong; nothing was changed. Inspect the new preview before confirming again. Feature apps use the same preview and confirmation protocol for irreversible operations.
Codes: `MissingParameter`, `InvalidParameterFormat`, `InvalidParameter`, `RecordNotFound`, `AmbiguousRecord`, `ConflictingIdentifiers`, `InvalidFilterField`, `InvalidLine`, `NothingToPreview`, `LinesSkipped`, `BlockedByWriteGuard`, `PreconditionFailed`, `PermissionDenied`, `LimitExceeded`, `BusinessCentralError`, `MultipleErrors`, `DeprecatedParameter`, `UnknownParameter`, `FieldChangedByBC`, `Retryable`, `EULA_REQUIRED`, `TRIAL_NOT_STARTED`, `ConfirmationRequired`, `ConfirmationMismatch`, `SecurityFilterApplied`. The `error` text may be translated; the code never is.

catalogue.name: Sales.Quote.Pdf
catalogue.description: Retrieves a sales quote as a PDF document and writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up.
catalogue.selectionDescription: Get a sales quote as a PDF file, printed with the customer's report selection (usage S.Quote). Takes a quote number or SystemId. The standard report may increase No. Printed and writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up.

strict.description: Optional root Boolean, default false. When true, unknown data keys are refused before execution with UnknownParameter. Do not place this option inside data.

subject.description: The quote number, or the SystemId of the sales quote.

target.description: A quote number, or a GUID read as the SystemId. Used when no data key names the quote.
The quote number. A GUID in this key is read as the SystemId.
The SystemId of the sales quote.

parameters.name: quoteNo
parameters.description: Quote number. A GUID is read as the SystemId. A sales order with the same number is not a quote.

parameters.name: quoteId
parameters.description: SystemId or quote number. Same resolution as quoteNo.

parameters.name: documentNo
parameters.description: Quote number or SystemId. Same resolution as quoteNo.

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: SystemId or quote number. Same resolution as quoteNo.

parameters.name: systemId
parameters.description: SystemId of the sales quote. A value that is not a GUID is refused.

parameters.name: recordSystemId
parameters.description: SystemId of the sales quote. Same rule as systemId.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: SystemId of the sales quote. Same rule as systemId.

fields.name: binary
fields.description: The sales quote PDF. The success body is the file itself, with content type application/pdf, not JSON.

errors.when: The caller has no read permission on Sales Header.
errors.fix: Ask an administrator for a permission set that reads the table.

errors.error: A sales quote number or SystemId is required.
errors.when: Neither subject nor a quote key was sent.
errors.fix: Send subject, quoteNo or systemId for one sales quote.

errors.when: The number or SystemId is not a sales quote. An order or another document is not a quote.
errors.fix: Check the quote number, or send the SystemId of a sales quote.

errors.error: The quote identifiers name different sales quotes.
errors.when: Two keys resolve to different quotes.
errors.fix: Send one quote number or one SystemId, or make every identifier name the same quote.

errors.when: The key is a number, boolean, object, array or null, or a SystemId key is not a GUID, or a number is longer than 20 characters.
errors.fix: Send the quote number as text of at most 20 characters, or a GUID SystemId.

errors.error: The sales quote PDF is empty.
errors.when: Report Selection usage S.Quote produced no bytes.
errors.fix: Check Report Selection usage S.Quote for the sell-to customer.

errors.when: No report is set up for usage S.Quote, or the report fails while rendering.
errors.fix: Check Report Selection usage S.Quote for the sell-to customer and the report layout.

errors.when: A transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. The error preserves Business Central's original text. Uncaught errors are Retryable only for types with effect write.
errors.fix: Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed.

effect.changes: Renders the sales quote with Report Selection usage S.Quote. The standard report may increase No. Printed and writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up. Saving the PDF commits the work done so far.

related.name: Sales.SalesInvoice.Pdf
related.useInsteadWhen: You need a posted sales invoice, not an open quote.

related.name: Orchestrator.Report.SaveAs
related.useInsteadWhen: You already know the report id and the table view, and you do not want the customer report selection.

steps.purpose: Get the PDF with the quote number or its SystemId.

chapters.overview: Returns one sales quote as a PDF file, printed with the report the customer's Report Selection (usage S.Quote, default report 1304) names. Send the quote number or the SystemId. Only a sales quote matches; a sales order with the same number does not. The standard report writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up.
chapters.notes: subject and the keys quoteNo, quoteId, documentNo, documentId, systemId, recordSystemId and id are all tried. A value that is a GUID is the SystemId. Anything else is the quote number, and only Document Type Quote matches. Two keys that name different quotes are ConflictingIdentifiers. One that matches nothing is RecordNotFound. Only the success answer is a PDF; an error answer is JSON. The same read-permission check as Sales.SalesInvoice.Pdf is applied to Sales Header. The standard report writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up. Saving the PDF commits the work done so far, so the call cannot run inside a larger transaction that is rolled back.

parameters.description: SystemId or quote number. Same resolution as quoteNo.

parameters.description: SystemId of the sales quote. Same rule as systemId.

parameters.description: SystemId of the sales quote. Same rule as systemId.

fields.name: binary

errors.when: The caller has no read permission on Sales Header.
errors.fix: Ask an administrator for a permission set that reads the table.

errors.error: A sales quote number or SystemId is required.
errors.when: Neither subject nor a quote key was sent.
errors.fix: Send subject, quoteNo or systemId for one sales quote.

errors.when: The number or SystemId is not a sales quote. An order or another document is not a quote.
errors.fix: Check the quote number, or send the SystemId of a sales quote.

errors.error: The quote identifiers name different sales quotes.
errors.when: Two keys resolve to different quotes.
errors.fix: Send one quote number or one SystemId, or make every identifier name the same quote.

errors.when: The key is a number, boolean, object, array or null, or a SystemId key is not a GUID, or a number is longer than 20 characters.
errors.fix: Send the quote number as text of at most 20 characters, or a GUID SystemId.

errors.when: Report Selection usage S.Quote produced no bytes.

errors.when: A transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. The error preserves Business Central's original text. Uncaught errors are Retryable only for types with effect write.
errors.fix: Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed.

effect.changes: Renders the sales quote with Report Selection usage S.Quote. The standard report may increase No. Printed and writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up. Saving the PDF commits the work done so far.

related.useInsteadWhen: You need a posted sales invoice, not an open quote.

related.name: Orchestrator.Report.SaveAs
related.useInsteadWhen: You already know the report id and the table view, and you do not want the customer report selection.

steps.purpose: Get the PDF with the quote number or its SystemId.

chapters.overview: Returns one sales quote as a PDF file, printed with the report the customer's Report Selection (usage S.Quote, default report 1304) names. Send the quote number or the SystemId. Only a sales quote matches; a sales order with the same number does not. The standard report writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up.
chapters.notes: subject and the keys quoteNo, quoteId, documentNo, documentId, systemId, recordSystemId and id are all tried. A value that is a GUID is the SystemId. Anything else is the quote number, and only Document Type Quote matches. Two keys that name different quotes are ConflictingIdentifiers. One that matches nothing is RecordNotFound. Only the success answer is a PDF; an error answer is JSON. The same read-permission check as Sales.SalesInvoice.Pdf is applied to Sales Header. The standard report writes an interaction log entry when an interaction template is set up. Saving the PDF commits the work done so far, so the call cannot run inside a larger transaction that is rolled back.
